clue.text: Vet slack film script

parts.note: to vet is to check over, as security staff screen candidates
slack in a rope is play, give or looseness

explanation.surface: An instruction to check a lazily written movie script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vet' and 'slack' look like verb and adjective describing the script; each is a synonym piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A screenplay is the written text a film is shot from, its script.

clue.text: Problem over wrestling style

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A difficulty concerning a particular way of wrestling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is the Japanese form of wrestling between heavyweight contestants.

clue.text: Studying danger at sea involving current

indicators.note: involving means including, so the mixed letters hold another inside
at sea means confused and muddled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: Researching the hazards of the ocean, including its currents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges DANGER and 'involving' adds I (current) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading a subject, in British usage, means studying it at university.

clue.text: Not difficult covering London landmark, pleasant to look at

parts.note: easy means not difficult
on means placed on top of, covering
The Eye, the London Eye, is the giant observation wheel on the Thames

explanation.surface: An undemanding tour of a famous London sight proves attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: THE EYE is the London Eye, a giant observation wheel on London's South Bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy on the eye is an idiom for attractive or good-looking.

clue.text: Expecting page on ruling

parts.note: regnant means reigning or ruling

explanation.surface: Anticipating a page about some legal ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruling' looks like a court decision but is the adjective REGNANT; 'on' places P on top in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Expecting is the polite idiom for carrying a baby, being with child.

clue.text: Set on having a little time on course

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a tack is a sailing course or line of action

explanation.surface: Being given a brief spell on a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: To set on someone means to assault them, to attack.

clue.text: Dishonest scheme of rascal cut short

indicators.note: cutting the word short removes its final letter

parts.note: a scamp is a mischievous rascal

explanation.surface: A rogue's crooked plan is foiled before it gets going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the last letter P from SCAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a fraudulent plot or swindle, a dishonest scheme.

clue.text: Ceremonial carriage coming from church, a striking display

parts.note: a riot of colour is a vivid, striking display

explanation.surface: A state coach leaves a church amid a dazzling show.
explanation.definitionFit: A chariot is a stately horse-drawn carriage used on ceremonial occasions.

clue.text: Object to supporting expert in TV show

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath, so comes second

parts.note: a master is an expert
to mind something is to object to it

explanation.surface: Taking issue with an authority propping up a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts MIND underneath MASTER in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastermind is a long-running BBC quiz programme with its famous black chair.

clue.text: Statesmen failed to hold small financial checks

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the extra letter within them
letters of a word that has failed are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Politicians flunk modest assessments of their own finances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failed' is the anagram signal and 'to hold' the insertion signal; 'small' gives S, as on clothing labels.
explanation.definitionFit: Means tests assess a person's income and assets to decide eligibility for benefits, so they are checks on finances.

clue.text: Money runs out for swimmer

indicators.note: the runs go out of the word for money, leaving it

parts.note: brass is northern British slang for money
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone's cash runs dry, so they take to the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes R (runs) from BRASS, British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The bass is a fish, and crosswords often call any fish a swimmer.

clue.text: Bar led lads astray about noughts and crosses

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the mixed letters go round others
letters gone astray have wandered out of order

parts.note: noughts are zeros, each written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Boys led out of the pub start a game of noughts and crosses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges BAR LED LADS and 'about' puts it round OO. 'Noughts and crosses' (tic-tac-toe) looks like one phrase; 'crosses' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Labradoodles are crossbred dogs, labrador crossed with poodle, so they are crosses.

clue.text: Storage chamber, likewise, enthralling the Italian

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so one word holds the other inside

parts.note: so means likewise, as in 'and so did I'
il is the Italian masculine definite article

explanation.surface: A storeroom similarly captivates an Italian man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralling' signals insertion; 'the Italian' is the Italian article, not an Italian person.
explanation.definitionFit: A silo is a tower or pit for storing grain, fodder or missiles, a storage chamber.

clue.text: Working in a centre for fruit

indicators.note: letters that are worked are kneaded into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone employed at a centre that deals in fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' rearranges the nine letters of IN A CENTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach, a fruit.

clue.text: Soar past broken-down thing, unreliable

parts.note: to soar is to fly
by means past, as in 'walk by'

indicators.note: something broken down is in pieces, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Swooping over a wrecked contraption that cannot be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken-down' rearranges THING into NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly-by-night outfit is shady and untrustworthy, likely to vanish overnight.

clue.text: Illumination coming from fire in grate, primarily

parts.note: to fire something is to light it

indicators.note: primarily means taking just the first letter of the word that follows it

explanation.surface: Light given off by a fire burning in a hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes G, the first letter of 'grate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighting is the provision of light, which is illumination.

clue.text: Prime Minister must accept rubbish start to election for now

indicators.note: the abbreviation takes in other letters, opening up to hold them

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A leader has to put up with nonsense as the campaign begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must accept' signals insertion and 'start to' takes a first letter; 'Prime' belongs to the abbreviation, not a selection.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro tem, short for the Latin pro tempore, means temporarily, for the time being.

clue.text: Ban for husband took effect after one

indicators.note: after means the piece comes later than the one named next

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
I is the Roman numeral one
a measure that bit took effect, as when brakes bite

explanation.surface: A prohibition supporting a husband finally took hold after one attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places BIT after I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: To prohibit something is to forbid it, imposing a ban.

clue.text: Busy person going about work with quiet shepherdess

indicators.note: going about means surrounding, so these letters wrap round others

parts.note: a busy bee is a hard-working person
OP is short for opus, a work
P stands for piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: An energetic worker doing her job quietly among the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going about' signals insertion; OP is opus and P is piano, the musical term for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Bo-Peep is the nursery-rhyme shepherdess who lost her sheep.

clue.text: Fizzy drink with my northern cinema fare?

parts.note: pop is a fizzy soft drink
cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'

explanation.surface: A soda and an exclamation from someone in the north at the pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation like 'my!' or 'gosh!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Popcorn is the classic snack sold and eaten at the cinema, so cinema fare.

clue.text: Greek papers and press showing American sports field

parts.note: ID means identity papers
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: A Greek's documents and ironing reveal a US stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'papers' as ID is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Gridiron is the name for an American football field, from its grid of yard lines.

clue.text: Followers reunite, intoxicated

indicators.note: intoxicated means drunk and reeling, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Fans get together again and get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intoxicated' rearranges REUNITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the group of attendants who follow an important person.

clue.text: Departed hastily, we hear, following staff complaint that's exaggerated

indicators.note: following means coming after the piece named next

parts.note: to man is to staff, so man stands for staff

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is spoken, giving another of the same sound

parts.note: flew means rushed away, departed hastily

explanation.surface: Someone rushed off after an employee grumbled about overblown complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' signals a sound-alike and 'following' sets the order; 'staff' is a verb here, to crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Man flu is a jokey term for a mild cold that men supposedly exaggerate into a serious illness.

clue.text: One of baby's complaints — any perhaps treated out East?

indicators.note: letters that are treated are processed and reworked into a new order
the letter for East is left out of the rearranged pool

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A rash on an infant, perhaps cured with eastern remedies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' shuffles ANY PERHAPS and 'out' drops E (East) from those ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nappy rash is skin irritation from a wet diaper, a common infant complaint.

clue.text: Expletive coming from boathouse

indicators.note: the letters come straight out of the middle of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A curse heard from inside a riverside shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming from' hides the answer in bOATHouse.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a swear word, so an expletive.

clue.text: Timber trade

definitions.meaning: fir or pine wood cut into planks
to do business, buy and sell

explanation.definitionFit: Deal is softwood timber in planks, and to deal is to trade, as a dealer does.

clue.text: Produce good line

parts.note: a row is a line of things side by side

explanation.surface: A command to grow fine rows of vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce' reads as a noun for vegetables but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow crops is to produce them, cultivating and bringing them on.

clue.text: Leaving rest unprepared

parts.note: to be off is to leave or depart
the balance is the rest or remainder

explanation.surface: Abandoning the remainder without any preparation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rest' means remainder here, not repose.
explanation.definitionFit: Being off balance means caught unawares, so unprepared for something.

clue.text: Fish in barrel at front of aquarium

parts.note: a tun is a large barrel or cask

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fish swims in a barrel at the front of the aquarium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at front of' takes A from 'aquarium'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large sea fish of the mackerel family.

clue.text: Fortunate, a short time before, also

parts.note: just means very recently, as in 'he has just left'
as well means also or too

explanation.surface: Lucky, a moment earlier, too.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is just as well means it is lucky or fortunate it happened.
